<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|346|THE ACTES|CHA. XVIII.}}</noinclude>he disputed in the synagogue euery Sabboth, interposing the name of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}}, and he exhorted the Iewes and the Greekes. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=5}}† And vvhen Silas and Timothee vvere come from Macedonia, Paul vvas instant in preaching, testifying to the Iewes that {{sc|Iesvs}} is {{sc|Christ}}. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=6}}† But they contradicting and blaspheming, he shaking his garments, said to them, Your bloud vpon your ovvne head: I being cleane, from hence forth vvil goe to the Gentiles. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=7}}† And departing thence, he entred into the house of a certaine man, named Titus Iustus, one that serued God, vvhose house vvas adioyning to the synagogue. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=8}}† And Crispus the prince of the Synagogue beleeued our Lord, vvith al his house: and many of the Corinthians hearing beleeued, and vvere baptized. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=9}}† And our Lord said in the night by a vision to Paul, Doe not feare, but speake, and hold not thy peace, {{verse|chapter=18|verse=10}}† for-because I am vvith thee: and no man shal set vpon thee to hurt thee: for I haue much people in this citie. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=11}}† And he sate there a yere & sixe moneths, teaching among them the vvord of God. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=12}}† But Gallio being Proconsul of Achaia, the Iewes vvith one accord rose vp against Paul, and brought him to the iudgement seate, {{verse|chapter=18|verse=13}}† saying, That this man contrarie to the Law persuadeth men to worshippe God. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=14}}† And Paul beginning to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Iewes, If it vvere some vniust thing, or an heinous facte, O you men Iewes, I should by reason beare you. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=15}}† But if they be questions of vvord & names, and of your law, your selues looke vnto it: I vvil not be iudge of these things. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=16}}† And he droue them from the iudgement seate. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=17}}† And al apprehending Sósthenes the prince of the synagogue, strooke him before the iudgement seate: and Gallio cared for none of those things.

{{verse|chapter=18|verse=18}}† But Paul vvhen he had staied yet many daies, taking his leaue of the brethren, sailed to Syria, (and vvith him Priscilla and Aquila,) vvho had shorne his head in Cenchris. for he had {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Nu. 6, 18. Act. 21, 24.''}}* a vow. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=19}}† And he came vnto Ephesus, and them he left there. But him self entring into the synagogue, disputed vvith the Iewes. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=20}}† And vvhen they desired him, that he would tarie a longer time, he consented not, {{verse|chapter=18|verse=21}}† but taking his leaue, and saying, I vvil returne to you againe God vvilling, he departed from Ephesus. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=22}}† And going dovvne to Cæsaréa, he vvent vp, and saluted the Church, and came downe to Antioche.<noinclude>{{rh|||And}}</noinclude>
